svg.title: Bench Readings vs. Pass Limits
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-bench-readings-vs-limits; chapter number: 4; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Bench Readings vs. Pass Limits; subtitle: Measured values against thresholds on the electrical safety sequence; total range: Measured reading (low) against pass or fail threshold (high), per test; caption: Prove the analyzer first, then run mains, protective earth, leakage and insulation in a fixed sequence; Josh Herzka's R Series defib passed both leakage checks with wide margin.; assumptions note: Each bucket carries its own unit as stated in the notes; buckets are compared within a test, not across tests.; note: Attributed to Josh Herzka of ReNew Biomedical on the Better Biomed Channel, and to AbishkarTECH on the Fluke ESA620.; buckets: label: Earth leakage, R Series defib; low: 129; high: 500; notes: Microamps; 129 measured under normal conditions vs an under-500 limit.; label: Applied-part leakage, single fault; low: 6.5; high: 50; notes: Microamps; 6.5 measured vs a limit of 50.; label: Mains check on a no-ground fault; low: 32; high: 53; notes: Neutral-to-earth 32 and live-to-earth 53 vs an expected figure under five.; label: Insulation resistance; low: 2; high: 100; notes: Megohms; below 2 fails, 1.5 fails, OL over the 100 megohm range is good.
